front.title: Merkle-Anchored Model Weight Release and RATS-Attested Runtime Activation Binding for Edge and Cloud AI Fleets

abstract.t: Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust (SCITT) provides transparent artifact statements, and Remote Attestation Procedures (RATS, RFC 9334) provide hardware/runtime attestation evidence. However, no existing internet standard defines an atomic cryptographic binding between a chunked AI model weight release manifest, a hardware-monotonic anti-rollback epoch counter, and a live RATS attestation result at the moment model weights are mapped into accelerator memory. This document specifies the Model Activation Binding Token (MABT) protocol, preventing load-time weight substitution, silent quantization downgrade, and rollback attacks across cloud and edge AI inference fleets.

section.name: Introduction and Problem Statement
section.t: AI model weights (GGUF, Safetensors, ONNX) are multi-gigabyte artifacts loaded dynamically by agent runtimes. Standard container image signing verifies the container binary at boot, but does not cryptographically bind the active model tensor chunks, LoRA adapter layers, and quantization profile in GPU/NPU memory to a SCITT transparency receipt and a RATS hardware nonce during inference execution.

This specification complements the foundational execution-trace verification architecture defined in draft-durga-agenttrust-trace-verification-00 by introducing deterministic, fail-closed wire semantics specifically addressing Merkle Model Activation Binding.

section.name: Normative Fail-Closed Verification Rules
section.t: Conforming verifiers and relying-party gateways MUST enforce the following deterministic invariants before releasing any downstream side effect:

ol.li: CHUNKED_WEIGHT_MERKLE_VERIFICATION: The weight_merkle_root MUST be computed as a binary Merkle tree (RFC 9162 style domain separation: 0x00 for leaves, 0x01 for internal nodes) over ordered, fixed-size tensor chunks prior to DMA transfer into accelerator memory.

ANTI_ROLLBACK_EPOCH_ENFORCEMENT: Conforming verifiers MUST reject any MABT whose anti_rollback_security_epoch is strictly less than the minimum security epoch persisted in hardware NVRAM or the fleet policy ledger.
RATS_NONCE_FRESHNESS: The rats_eat_attestation_hash MUST bind the runtime's hardware measurement, weight_merkle_root, and activation_nonce so replayed attestations from prior boot cycles fail closed.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: All pre-image objects MUST be canonicalized using RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) prior to signature generation or verification under RFC 8032 Ed25519. Any clock skew exceeding 60 seconds, digest mismatch, or missing cryptographic binding MUST cause the verifier to fail closed and emit an auditable security rejection receipt.
